item.text: The fuzz harness failed in harness code (nil leader → panic in `fuzzy`'s own `WaitTilUptoDate`), preceded by "RPC does not have a header" — an incompatibility between the old fuzzy harness and newer raft, not the store swap. Let me record this attempt honestly.

Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

This turn I made a genuine attempt at the one remaining independent method: the repository's own randomized fuzz harness in `fuzzy/`, which is a separate module written against raft v1.2.0 and can't build offline (missing `raft-boltdb`/`boltdb`). I stubbed those in a scratch copy (`work/_scratch_fuzzy/`) — in-memory store instead of BoltStore, go-msgpack/v2 pinned to the cached v2.1.2, and `replace github.com/hashicorp/raft => ../..` pointing at the audited module — got it to build and `go vet` cleanly against the audited code, then ran `TestRaft_NoIssueSanity`.

It failed, but the failure is in the **harness, not in raft**: no leader was ever elected (the log is full of `failed to make requestVote RPC ... error="RPC does not have a header"`), so the harness's `WaitTilUptoDate` dereferenced a nil leader and panicked. The `"RPC does not have a header"` error originates in `raft.checkRPCHeader` and reflects an incompatibility between the old fuzzy transport/verifier and current raft — not my store substitution, which only affects log/stable storage. I recorded this honestly as **inconclusive, not evidence of a defect**, with the log at `audit-evidence/fuzzy_sanity.log` and the scratch setup preserved under `work/_scratch_fuzzy/` for anyone who has the real dependencies or a version-matched harness.

No change to the audit's conclusions:

- One confirmed defect: `testing.go`'s `cluster.EnsureSamePeers` freezes its reference peer set outside its retry loop, causing intermittent false `peer mismatch` failures in three shipped tests on a healthy cluster; mechanism-verified and causally validated by a one-line fix (re-tested cases → 0/20).
- No consensus-level defect across complete source review plus five independent behavioral methods (~16k acked commands, zero divergence, zero loss).
- One open item, stated plainly: whether that helper is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake, unresolvable offline because the module cache's sumdb records don't verify and no pristine reference is reachable.

The captured implementation remains unmodified (`diff -rq source work` clean; `go vet ./...` passes), and all reproduction artifacts are preserved under `work/`.
